behaviour: Card drawing code comes from the diagram mod, which exposes its parser and renderer for plumb's plugin to call.
Removing a link renumbers the later links down by one and the command prints every new number.
The agent may remove or move a link with a logged note, but removing a confirmed example's only live test is refused.
The judge's goes-beyond and contradicts findings reach the owner as one line on the request's read-back card.
A merge conflict is answered on its card or through the agent in chat, applied only when the owner clearly picks a version.
The browser is first an issue-resolution workspace where the owner understands, answers and follows repairs of issues.
The browser workspace resolves each kind of Plumb issue within one project, leaving team coordination to the harness.
note: Agent-integration question reopened; scope part holds.

behaviour: Browser issue resolution follows existing card and mod behaviour, including the connection to agent follow-up.
Sonnet is an optional judge for judging runs while JEV/Haiku remain available.
JEV's choice output stays supported as a configuration despite judging worse than yes/no.
Only what plumb itself saw counts as the owner's answer: a card press, a typed command, or the owner's message read against the question.
Intent is analysed only when the owner uses a command; ordinary messages run no model.
The agent receives everything as text while the owner sees cards only, and the full/compact/off setting is retired.
When no judge is reachable plumb says so once and blocks only steps needing a judge, deciding nothing by rule.
Changes to code or tests linked to a confirmed requirement never ask the owner by default; plumb checks coverage and repins.
Remaining browser work continues on its feature branch worktree, committed per task.
note: Branch-location instruction for finishing one task.

behaviour: A hook is cut by a configurable watchdog hard limit defaulting to 6 s, with soft budgets near 4 s.
note: DEC-078 states 30 s limit and says it replaces this.

behaviour: Verdicts form a cascade: JEV above its threshold decides and may auto-approve, otherwise the judge model decides for cards and tidying.
note: Already folds in DEC-073's model-verdict rule.

behaviour: A retired example is gone: its test is unmarked or deleted and the superseding record keeps only what it states.
Links stale from before the drift gate get one baseline repin pass, with untested ones judged on meaning and carded by record.
Every edit to a confirmed record needs owner reconfirmation, asked once per principle with derived records listed.
When a judge job is only partly answered, existing verdicts apply at once and only the rest waits with one explanatory line.
The judge_model setting governs verdicts, their evaluation run and the fingerprint, while understand.model reads the owner's words.
A message that does only part of what the reader looks for has its clear part applied and only the unclear part asked.
Browser workspace tests are collected only when the tests/browser directory is named or --browser is passed.
note: Merge-conflict choice; behaviour lives in SR-184.

behaviour: All of the clarifier's blocking questions are specific and asked with Claude Code's question tool.
A judge model's verdict may confirm requirements and decisions grounded in the owner's verified words, marked and reversible, never intents.
A worktree reads the owner's prompt text from the main checkout's session log via git's common directory.
The verdict judge is a cascade of JEV first then a judge model, per the open-items branch wording.
The clarifier change is built after the browser merge lands, as its own branch.
Background plumb processes on Windows use CREATE_NO_WINDOW with CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP, never DETACHED_PROCESS.
Hooks are cut by a 30 s watchdog with soft budgets of 20 s and 5 s, plus set limits for tests, judge and git, all settings.
The intent loop runs on command while ordinary work keeps the background grounding loop.
The owner opens the intent loop by typing /plumb intent.
Clarification and integration against the records run as one intent loop with one judge gate.
Each stage's review is enforced by stage commands refusing to run without the previous passed gate; hooks only close the edit gate and hold merges.
The record set is rebuilt as a short version 2 with old records retired by a supersedes trail.
note: The rebuild task itself, now underway.

behaviour: A requirement is one durable observable behaviour with examples and a proof, fixes go under their requirement, and an intent is one per principle.
The done work lands on the owner's word with per-record holds bypassed and logged and the owner confirming the set once.
note: One-time landing of the browser merge.

behaviour: Superseded branches are integrated or dropped: proof-findings integrated, cascade logs merged, leftovers dropped.
Conflicting panel and agent-brief tests stay failing until the rewrite states panel and agent behaviour once.
When a newer owner decision changes a behaviour an older example's test asserts, the tests follow the newer decision.
A refused automatic approval reported by validate is left as it is until the rewrite states confirmation once.
